title: Console walkthrough: Usage analytics + per-route dashboards + cost breakdown - EdenCare Health
summary: Redwood AE+SE demo of Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for sensitive PHI workloads; key concerns: data residency, SOC2/KMS, and cost per route for multi-model pipeline. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with sample traffic and share security docs + pricing.
topics: Security controls: SOC 2, SAML, KMS, VPC/private deployment
next_steps: Jordan Kim - Send dedicated vs hosted pricing sheet and pilot contract (due 2026-06-04)
Priya Raman - Share benchmark spreadsheet and Console guide links (due 2026-05-31)
Laura Chen - Provide sample anonymized traffic and list of key routes for pilot (due 2026-06-02)
Sam Ortiz - Share internal security questionnaire; Redwood to respond (due 2026-06-07)
Schedule pilot kickoff call w/ infra team (tentative 2026-06-08)
action_items: Jordan Kim - Prepare pricing + committed capacity options
Priya Raman - Export per-route demo dashboards as PDF and share
Evan Cole - Help instrument sample SDK calls for pilot
Laura Chen - Send list of endpoints and expected qps for pilot
Sam Ortiz - Confirm if KMS/HSM required or KMS is OK
transcript:
Header: 2026-05-28 15:00 PST | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Evan Cole (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (CTO - EdenCare), Laura Chen (Head of ML Ops), Sam Ortiz (Security), Nina Patel (PM)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Kim from Redwood inference, and with me is Priya and Evan who will run through the Console demo - we'll focus on usage analytics and per-route cost break downs that you asked about.
[00:14] Mark: Great thanks Jordan, we have about 50 minutes, want to make sure we cover security questions too, Sam is here for that.
[00:22] Priya: Awesome, quick agenda: overview of Console, live demo of per-route dashboards, cost breakdown and unit economics, then Q&A and pilot next steps.
[00:35] Nina: one quick thing, our main use case is clinical triage and note summarization, lots of PHI, so data residency and audit logs are must-haves.
[00:45] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll highlight audit logs and KMS options during the demo - and we'll show the dedicated capacity flow as well.
[01:02] Priya: jumping in - here's the Console home, you can see usage overview, tokens in/out, latency percentiles. The left nav has Routes -> that's where you configure per-route settings and see per-route dashboards.
[01:28] [01:28] Priya: (mouse noise) clicking into Routes, we have a route for note-summarization, another for triage-classifier, and a rerank route. On the top we switch time window, breakdown by model, and by deployment (hosted vs dedicated).
[01:50] Laura: how granular is the cost breakdown? can we get cost per request per route?
[01:55] Priya: yes - we show cost per 1k tokens, cost per request, and aggregated cost by route and by model. here's an example: note-summarization is heavy on output tokens so the per-request cost is ~ $0.14 on the current small model, while triage-classifier is cheaper but high qps. note: these numbers reflect our list-price and don't include committed discounts.
[02:22] Mark: okay and does that account for KV cache hits and batching savings?
[02:27] Priya: good question - yes, the dashboard has toggles to show raw token cost versus effective cost after prefix/KV cache hits and batching. you can filter the view to only cache hits or misses. sometimes the transcription omitted 'KV' as 'K V cash' but it's the same metric.
[03:00] Evan: you can also drill into a single request timeline - shows model selection, kernels used, and a rough latency breakdown: model compute vs network vs queuing. this is handy for SLA discussions.
[03:20] Sam: from a security standpoint - how are logs stored, and can we ship logs to our SIEM? we can't retain PHI in third-party logs unless encrypted + access controlled.
[03:34] Jordan: we support audit log forwarding to your SIEM and we have an option to redact PII at ingest. For Private deployments you can keep logs on your VPC. We support KMS for key management and also HSM integrations for enterprise.
[03:50] Sam: do you have SOC 2 and ISO attestations?
[03:53] Jordan: yes SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 - we'll send the attestation and our security questionnaire.
[04:10] Priya: back to the dashboard - here's per-route SLO tracking. You can set a latency SLO, and the Console will show percentage of requests meeting that SLO, and you can tie on-call alerts. there's also a cost guardrail so you can set per-route budgets.
[04:37] Laura: Budget guardrails seems useful - can we automatically fallback to a cheaper model when a route exceeds cost or latency thresholds?
[04:45] Priya: yep, routing policies allow fallback to cheaper model variants or a lower-capacity tier. in the Console you can define a policy: if latency > 800ms for 5m, switch to model-x-quantized. this is great for graceful degradation.
[05:06] Mark: what's the overhead for quantized models? do you see hallucination/regression risk?
[05:12] Priya: there is a tradeoff - our Optimize tool recommends quantization profiles per workload and runs evals. the Console integrates quality monitoring so if you see regression in key prompts the system can alert or roll back. we usually recommend a small eval set to validate.
[05:34] [05:34] (crosstalk) Nina: so for the pilot we'll run 3 routes - note-summarization, triage-classifier, and a patient-match endpoint.
[05:45] Evan: perfect, on the pilot we can preconfigure the routes and add synthetic traffic. we'll also enable per-route cost sampling so you get a clear baseline.
[06:10] Priya: demonstrating the cost breakdown export - you can export CSV with per-route token counts, model used, effective cost after caching and batching, and a projected monthly cost based on current qps.
[06:30] Mark: can you show the token-level breakdown? our finance team wants line-item visibility for token generation vs embeddings.
[06:37] Priya: sure - toggle Embeddings vs Generation. embeddings show a separate meter and cost line on the route dashboard. you can also tag requests with metadata (e.g., pii=true) to filter cost by data sensitivity.
[06:56] Sam: tagging sounds good but who ensures tags are correct? we need enforced routing rules so PHI always stays in private deployment.
[07:05] Jordan: you can add rules at the API gateway level - enforce route-level policies so any request with pii=true is routed to Dedicated or Private. we can show rule examples in the pilot.
[07:20] Priya: switching to the usage heatmap - this helps identify peak windows and tail latency. the Console automatically suggests autoscaling knobs for Dedicated pools based on historical qps and P95 latencies.
[07:40] Laura: we have bursty traffic eod every day, will Dedicated handle bursts or do we need burst capacity?
[07:48] Evan: Dedicated supports configurable burst capacity and we can set burst percentage. plus routing policies can spill to hosted if you allow it for non-PHI traffic.
[08:05] Mark: pricing - what does committed capacity look like, and how much discount?
[08:12] Jordan: committed capacity pricing varies by GPU family and term. for example, a 3-month reserve on A100-like dedicated units gives ~25% off API list price; longer commitments increase discounts. we'll send a detailed sheet.
[08:30] Nina: can we get sample invoices or per-route billing statements?
[08:34] Jordan: yes Console has a Billing -> Per-route billing export. you can also get token-level line items per day.
[08:45] Priya: demoing Incident timeline view - if a regression is detected, the system ties errors to recent model rollouts and shows which routes were affected. this makes root cause faster.
[09:05] Sam: about data residency - can data be pinned by region? we need EU data to stay in EU.
[09:12] Jordan: yes region pinning supported, and Private deployments can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem. we also support customer-managed keys with region-aware KMS.
[09:30] Mark: curious about observability retention - how long do you keep detailed request traces?
[09:36] Priya: default is 30 days for detailed traces, but you can purchase extended retention as an add-on for compliance or audits.
[09:50] Laura: for the pilot we'd like 90-day retention for certain routes.
[09:55] Jordan: we can add that as an add-on on the pilot contract.
[10:05] [10:05] Priya: switching to a troubleshooting scenario - triage route saw high P95, here's an example: large prompt size, no KV cache hit, and spike in batch queue. resolving it: enable prefix caching on that route and increase batch concurrency; Console shows predicted cost impact.
[10:35] Mark: how accurate are predicted cost savings? our CFO wants conservative estimates.
[10:40] Priya: predictions are based on historical distribution of prompt lengths and cache hit rates; we provide a range (best/expected/worst) so finance can use conservative numbers.
[11:00] Nina: regarding integrations, do you have SSO? we need SAML + SCIM for provisioning.
[11:06] Jordan: yes SAML + SCIM supported, RBAC in Console, and audit logs for admin actions. we'll share the SSO setup guide.
[11:20] Sam: one more security ask - do you support per-request encryption with our KMS?
[11:25] Jordan: yes per-request envelope encryption supported with customer KMS; if you need HSM-backed keys we can support that too under enterprise plan.
[11:40] Priya: near the end here - recap of pilot: 2-week pilot, three routes, sample traffic, enable audit log forwarding, 90-day retention for pilot routes, routing rules to keep PHI in Private/Dedicated.
[11:58] Mark: timeline looks good, we'll confirm internal stakeholders and send sample traffic.
[12:05] Jordan: great - we'll share pricing sheet and security docs after this call. any final q's?
[12:14] (short silence)
[12:18] Nina: nope thanks, appreciate the thorough demo.
[12:22] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the next steps.
